utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: While the witness is coming into court, let me announce a slight alteration to the sitting schedule. We'll sit until 10.30 for the first session this morning and then from 11.00 for the second session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your examination by Mr. Visnjic will continue in a moment, but please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you made at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to that evidence today. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Before I continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I continue examining General Gajic, Your Honours, I would like to tell you that we have looked at your suggestion concerning the examination-in-chief of this witness, and during the night we have reorganised our direct. So this time we're going to focus on the material that we have, and in this way we are going to present through exhibits to the Trial Chamber certain activities in Kosovo that took place in 1998 and 1999. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday you told us about the activities that the Kosovo Liberation Army carried out in 1998 and 1999. We subdivided these periods in three phases, up to March 1998; the second one from March 1998 to October 1998; and the third one from November 1998 until the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: This time I would like us to go through some exhibits. I have categorised them in a way. I would like us to go through some parts of these documents, and I would like to ask you for your comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may I just note that the witness in his statement 3D1084, he made certain comments regarding these exhibits. However, now we've classified them according to subjects, topics. Also what I wish to say to you is that for the presentation here today in court, due to the brevity of time, we selected only a few, 327, characteristic events that took place. As for the other things that happened, they are represented in the documents and we would like the Trial Chamber to examine them in their entirety at a later stage. Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 3D993, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which page of the statement does that one refer to, Mr. Visnjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness commented on these exhibits in paragraphs 17 through -- 17 through 134.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We, but 3D -- yes, you're starting with the one in paragraph 17?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. This time I've divided it according to topics. I think that that will be easier for you to follow. At any rate, we will try to strike a balance between what the statement says and what the witness is going to testify to during his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, yesterday as you were waiting in front of the courtroom, another witness spoke about Grom 98, plan Grom 98. In one paragraph of this plan it says that the army -- that the Army of Yugoslavia defines certain activities in Kosovo as a purported humanitarian catastrophe. My question is: Did the Army of Yugoslavia have any reason to call events in Kosovo a purported humanitarian catastrophe?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did have reason to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at paragraph 2 of 3D993.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a report from the security section of the Pristina Corps dated the 31st of May, 1998. And in paragraph 2 what is stated is that women and children have been moved from the territory of the municipality of Djakovica deeper inside Kosovo and Metohija or through identified illegal channels to Montenegro, because Montenegro was one of the transit areas and also a base where even members of the KLA sought shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, actually these are paragraphs 1 and 2, but wasn't one of the KLA tactics, or rather, what was the KLA tactic at the time that the VJ believed they were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is precisely what I wanted to say. This relocation of women and children further into the territory of Kosovo and Metohija or to Montenegro was a planned, organised, activity of the KLA in order for them to later portray this in the media as being carried out because of the excessive use of force and that the army and the MUP were to be blamed for that. So there were a great many such activities. And in actual fact they, the KLA, were doing this in a planned fashion. They were moving them deeper into Kosovo and across the border into Albania, Montenegro, even into Macedonia, their women and children, that is, and then by way of propaganda, through the media, they were saying that this was a humanitarian catastrophe. That is the core of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us a few things about this document, can you tell us some more about what kind of report is this?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a telegram that was sent by the commander of the Pristina Corps because sometime from June 1998 in the security administration on the orders of the then-chief, General Dimitrijevic, in order to have the security administration receive information about the situation in Kosovo as soon as possible because the situation was really changing fast, General Dimitrijevic decided and ordered that the security section of the Pristina Corps should daily provide information to the security administration about what was going on by way of telegrams. One copy of the telegram, in order not to hinder the chain of command, would be sent to the command of the Pristina Corps, rather, the 3rd Army and this went on all the way up to the 20th or the 21st of March, 1999, when the new chief of the security administration, General Geza Farkas, ordered that the telegrams be stopped. The security section of the Pristina Corps sent all of them -- their telegrams to the security department of the 3rd Army, and they in turn sent every day the so-called daily operations reports that contained not only the situation and the problems in Kosovo, but also in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, if I understood what you were saying, this is not a subject that I wanted to deal with now but perhaps we can clarify it now. There was one reporting system up to the beginning of the war and after the beginning of the war there was a different system of reporting?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Within the security organs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the security organs --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the speakers please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, I think it's important right at the outset that we set a tempo that the interpreters can cope with. It's important, Mr. Gajic, that since you're speaking the same language that you should wait until the translation is complete before you answer the question and you get a guide of that in front of you because once the translation is completed the cursor on the type writer will stop moving. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I'm going to make another suggestion. If you give shorter answers, we will automatically have a pause between questions and answers and that will be of assistance to the interpreters. My question was why at the beginning of the war a new reporting system was put in place within the security organs.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that the basic reason was the fact that the security organs of the Pristina Corps had a lot of work to do, and generally speaking that was the situation the beginning of the aggression of NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, I would like to ask you to look at Exhibit 3D994.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a document dated the 10th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I'm going to ask you to concentrate on paragraph 4 in Serbian that says: "In the forthcoming period, the KLA in the territory expects many asylum seekers to arrive from Europe via Albania in order to have more massive action in the territory," what is that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a fact that was confirmed several times through the reports, namely, that Albania was a destination where volunteers were gathered not only from Kosovo but from western European countries in terms of the militant political wing that existed in western Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to ask you to look at the next paragraph that says: "Yesterday's information about the moving out of women, children, and the elderly have been confirmed."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is to say that the information provided in the report of the previous day, the security organs checked that and confirmed that it was correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And all of that was happening in June, and as far as I can see in this paragraph these villages actually had not been emptied?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Who remained in the villages, General?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the KLA stayed in the villages, and probably part of the civilians who were some kind of logistics support. Just one more sentence. That is the time of intensive preparation and KLA activity that made it necessary to carry out an anti-terrorist operation at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It is the 12th of June, so 3D996 is our next document dated the 12th of June, 1998, paragraphs 6 and 7, or rather, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have page 2 of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have page 2 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we're in a different territory here, the municipality of Suva Reka, where yet again it is stated, as they say here in the document: "Siptar women and children were moved out," and what was continued was the building of shelters and in these two villages there were about 1.000 terrorists. What did this mean for the security administration at the time?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means that it was a confirmation of the previously commented upon information and other similar information that we had received; namely, that members of the KLA, while preparing for a clash with the MUP and the Army of Yugoslavia, were moving out their civilians in a planned fashion, that is to say to different areas, that they engage part of them for fortifying the area and they even engaged children which is in contravention of the Geneva Conventions. I'm sorry, let me finish. Here you can also see that they are carrying out organised preparations for a clash with the security forces and that they're relocating the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to ask you to look at document 3D997, dated the 13th of June, 1998, paragraph 3, the last three lines that say: "Not accepting any kind of dialogue, their refusal to accept any kind of dialogue, the evacuation of women and children and the fact that the terrorists are trying to take the best possible conditions for an all-out clash with the MUP and VJ organs throughout the territory."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, it should be in front of you. The paragraph begins with the words "operativnim radom"?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what does it mean operational work?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means we obtained this intelligence from various sources and the military security service had very good sources and tried to verify all the intelligence before they were circulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So very briefly, the last three lines here.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here again we see the same problem of the evacuation, planned evacuation organised by the KLA, and the second thing here is that this militant wing that the KLA represented refused any dialogue, any political settlement for the Kosovo problem. They only wanted to use arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I would like you to look at the text three passages down. It begins with the words "komunikacija Kosovska Mitrovica" and it says here: "On the 12th of June all of the Serbian population moved out after Srbica, most of the Siptars from that town moved out going in the direction of Kosovska Mitrovica."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the Lap Operative Zone and this is a striking example, striking evidence of the Serbian population. It shows that they were moving out on a daily basis under this pressure, again from the area of the Srbica municipality, practically all of the Serbs moved out, moving to the area of Kosovska Mitrovica where --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, General, we're still waiting for the interpretation. It says here in the text that most of the Albanians moved out from that town, too?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that's what I wanted to say. Not only were Serbs under pressure, but also honest Albanians, and I said yesterday that many Albanians were actually opposed to terrorism and to armed violence that was to be used to achieve the political goals. And more or less they shared the fate of the Serbian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, the population did not flee in the face of the conflict. They fled, they moved out, because they were under pressure, there was pressure exerted. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're completely right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at Defence Exhibit 3D998, the last two passages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General don't we see an example here of terrorists exerting pressure on the villagers in order to force them to move out of their villages?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is one of the many such examples, and we can see here where the pressure is exerted on the Albanian population to move out of the villages and there were many examples where ultimatums were issued and deadlines were set: You have to move out by such and such date. If they failed to obey an armed group of the KLA would arrive and would warn again and tell the population that the ultimatum has to be honoured.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the last passage- and you just gave evidence about that, that moving out of the population was an activity that the KLA performed in a planned manner?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What did the KLA achieve by moving out those people, apart from getting an empty space where it could fight the army?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what it did get was in the sphere of the humanitarian catastrophe, so-called humanitarian catastrophe. It was one of their strategic goals because they wanted to paint this picture for the world, for the international community, that the Albanians in Kosovo and Metohija are victims of a genocidal policy where the Army of Yugoslavia and MUP participated actively.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, if you move the Albanian population from one area and have them go across the border into the Republic of Albania, as we see in this here example, what happens on the other side of the border? It is stated here that they are received in an organised manner. Could you please tell us what happened with the population, with the women, children, men?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can give you an answer to that. There was -- there was a really good organisation in place. When the Albanian population would come, various genders, various ages, then they would be classified. Men of military age would be sent to training camps. They would be given weapons and they would receive military training so that they could later join the KLA. The women and children would be separated and put into other reception centres, where their life and work would be organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, we looked at this document and it was dated --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move it up a little bit, scroll up, I think it is the 16th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at another document, it's dated one month later, that's 3D1000.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, this is the command of the 2nd Army.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't yet gotten this document on my screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I don't want us to comment on this document paragraph by paragraph, but I would like to ask you, if you can, to just tell us briefly what is this document about.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it confirms in the second and third paragraph starting with the words "illegal crossings," this confirms what I have just said about the reception of the civilians from Kosovo and Metohija and their classification with the men of military age going to training centres and women, children, and the elderly going to other places. Here we see what they say about the organisation of the training, and this is the result of an interrogation of two Albanians, Edmir Musaj is the son of a retired Sigurimi officer service, the Albanian Sigurimi service and we can see that the main training centre for the Albanians was Tropoje. There are actually two centres, one is the centre for training and the other is the logistics centre. This is where the command is located, the command that had links with Sali Berisha because the people working at the centre command were in regular contact with Sali Berisha, which all speaks to the fact that Sali Berisha at that time, he was the president of Albania at the time, that he supported, or rather, he was not the president of Albania, but he was a high-ranking political official, that he was behind the KLA and the separatist movement in Kosovo and Metohija. .

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, just a moment, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're waiting for the interpretation?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, we're waiting for the Judges to see page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So what happened with the people who completed their training?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people who completed their training had two options. One was to wait the call-up and then to move through illegal channels to Kosovo, to try and get into Kosovo, and join the KLA units depending on the areas from which they had come from to undergo training; or they would return to Kosovo immediately, where they would immediately join the units or go home and wait for the call-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now I would like --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, if I may say one more sentence. It is important to stress here because this -- the fact that this document shows that the officers of the Albanian army were actually conducting this training in those centres.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have Defence Exhibit 3D1001 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, this document is dated the 1st of August, 1998, so some ten days after the previous document that we looked at. Could you please look at paragraph 3 that begins with the words: "The women and children have fled from Junik ..." And could you please comment on this paragraph, in particular the last sentence in this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This, as you said, is a document dated the 1st of August. This is the time when the anti-terrorist operation was underway already, and this paragraph shows us two things. First, that -- you have to know that Junik was a major stronghold of the KLA and they suffered some casualties because of the onslaught of the security forces and they were fleeing -- throwing down their arms and fleeing, trying to save their lives. And under the -- because of this action and because of the situation in the KLA, they were hiding their women and children, finding shelter for them, and in this column of women and children there were infiltrated terrorists. And some documents indicate that they even put on women's clothes in order to hide and to be able to move to other destinations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could we please look at the last paragraph on page 1, that's page 1 in the Serbian and in English that would be page 2, the penultimate paragraph. Here we have a description of the situation in the territory of another municipality, that of Glogovac, and it is stated here that the civilian population had been evacuated from that area, too; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, may I then conclude that both in the territory of Junik and Glogovac the civilian population was evacuated and combat, as indicated in this document, were either under way or were being prepared, rather, there were no civilians in that area during combat operations; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, you are absolutely right. I have to add one more thing. They created this psychological situation, and the desire, the fact, was to create this image of purported humanitarian catastrophe for the benefit of the international community. There -- even when there was no combat, when there were no combat operations, they would raise tensions, spread rumours that there would be attacks, and then they moved out the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. Mr. Gajic, just two questions. The paragraph you've just looked at actually says that the civilian population was evacuated because they expected a MUP attack, rather than to create some impression of humanitarian catastrophe because of refugees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I spoke in general about what they were doing, but in this specific case you are right. They expected the MUP to attack, and as far as I know this attack never materialised. But this psychological effect was being created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you've actually said that it was created in Glogovac, but it's difficult to draw that conclusion from this paragraph. The second question I want to ask you is this: What steps were taken to alter the impression that was abroad in the United Nations that the refugee problem was caused by Serb activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what the army did. I know that 3rd Army command, the Pristina Corps had some documents ordering that the Albanian people in the villages be contacted and inform that they were under no threat from the army and that they could feel safe and secure in this respect and that they were under threat of terrorism, that getting involved in terrorism was the real danger and despite the fact that these were different ethnicities --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not really my question. The evidence we have here is of an increasing impression over 1998 and early 1999 that the refugee crisis was caused by the activity of Yugoslav and Serb forces rather than the KLA. Now, what steps are you aware of taken by your government to create -- or to alter what you would say was a false impression that the international community had about the real source of the refugee problem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I know, although I don't really have any specific knowledge, but on the basis of what I do know representatives of the state organs and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in contacts with the international community tried to paint the real picture to tell the truth, and some publications were issued in order to inform the international community about the real state of affairs. I couldn't be more specific than that, but I do know that at this diplomatic level in all the contacts, efforts were made to explain what the essence of the problem in Kosovo and Metohija was when it comes to the civilian population, and indeed the overall situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, we have evidence that as early as the 31st of March the Security Council of United Nations in a resolution expressed the following: "Gravely concerned that the recent intense fighting in Kosovo and in particular the excessive and indiscriminate use of force by Serbian security forces and the Yugoslav Army, which have resulted in numerous civilian casualties and according to the estimate of the Secretary-General the displacement of over 230.000 persons from their homes." And I was really anxious to find out what the Serb authorities were going to correct what, according to you, is clearly a false impression. Now, are you aware of -- if you're not aware of any steps taken, then please simply say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, what I just said, this is the thing that I know of. I couldn't be more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to go back to a document we just looked at, document 3D996, to confirm what General Gajic just said about the efforts the army put in in order to keep the population in the territory, not to have them move out. And could we please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can certainly read it -- you've drawn our attention to it and we can read that for ourselves. If you're going to deal with the evidence in this way we're going to be here for many hours dealing with the statement and one wonders what's the point of the statement if you're going to elaborate on it and greatly expand the references to every incident that's simply summarized in three lines in the present statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I directly wanted to rely on General Gajic's answer. I wanted to indicate another paragraph that I didn't indicate before, and that is paragraph 3, that says that the villagers from Korenica -- could we please have that document on the screen, 3D996, which says briefly that the villagers of Korenica asked the Army of Yugoslavia for protection in order to be protected from terrorist attacks, and that therefore there were consultations going on with the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, sorry, I really have to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, please, now I would like to show 3D1002.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it has to do with population movements our one-but-last exhibit on that subject, 3D1002 dated the 9th of August, 1998, paragraph 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, do you see it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evacuation of members, is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you just give us a brief comment.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it confirms everything I've said so far. We see here that even a staff -- a KLA staff was established, headed by Tahir Zemaj, a former JNA officer, by the way, who was organising the transport of civilians, organised transport and evacuation, that is, towards Streocki Planine, the mountains of Streoc, and the border towards toward Montenegro that was a transit area, as I've already said; so they indeed have an organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let me correct one mistake I made. The resolution I was actually referring to was the 23rd of September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. This is our last exhibit on this topic, the 21st of August, 1998, 3D1004, points, or rather, point 2.1. In English it is probably -- yes, on this page, or rather, it would be good to move on to the next page in English. It's all right in Serbian, but perhaps I can read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: "In the woods between the villages of -- the villages of Duvnjak and Skivjane there are about 300 refugee from Junik and Glodjane. Some members of the KLA from these villages are among them and they are not allowing the civilians to return to their places of residence."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want my comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, a brief comment from you, please.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was several pieces of information of this nature where representatives of the KLA did not allow civilians to return to their places of residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the next topic that I would like us to deal with in this period from March to October, that is, pertaining to KLA activity are -- typical terrorist activities that they were carrying out, two exhibits 994 and 996 respectively. We are doing to start with 3D994.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I'd like to draw your attention to these paragraphs that are somewhere around the middle of the page in Serbian starting with the words: "On the 8th of June ..." In English it's page 1, we see it, and then it continues on page 2.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's these two paragraphs that speak of arming the KLA in the area. This is the territory of Metohija, or rather, the Dukajgin Operation Zone. Most probably they are arming the population by force because in the second paragraph there is a reference to the arming of the Catholic population. I know that there is a document among the evidence where it says that the Catholic population refused to take arms and that a Catholic priest opposed that and was therefore threatened by death. And that is why the Catholic population voluntarily surrendered their weapons to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you just give us your brief comment on the last two paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that this is psychological manipulation yet again pertaining to the 15th of June, 1998. They're saying that they're expecting an imminent threat of war to be declared and that their duty is to destroy everything Serbian, which is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, two paragraphs down it is stated that there is information concerning terrorist intentions of attacking Morina from Albania and from our territory. I'm not going to ask you much about border incidents. Colonel Cucak spoke about that when we started our Defence case, but this information, to have a border post attacked both from the territory of Albania and from the territory of Yugoslavia, what does that say to you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It tells us about synchronisations, and that was something that Colonel Cucak spoke about, that is what led to the extension of the border area twice. Synchronisation from the territory of Albania and supporters of the KLA from our area, our border area, that is to say from the territory of Metohija who were involved in these illegal channels, regarding the smuggling of weapons, military equipment, and terrorists. That is why, as I said the border belt was extended.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And our last exhibit related to these activities and the border 3D1001, paragraphs 4 through 7. That is the second half of this document. There is a rather interesting reference concerning a rather interesting way of how armed groups were being brought into the territory of Yugoslavia, or rather, Kosovo when the border belt was expanded. So it's the bottom of the page, the lower half of the text.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does it start?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: "It is expected that the bringing in of two numerous and well-armed groups of KLA members ..."

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what referred to, these illegal channels not only from Albania but also from Macedonia. I think I've said that there were channels from Macedonia, too. We identified seven channels through which weapons and military equipment and terrorists were brought in from the Republic of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, in this way we would conclude our review of KLA activity through these documents, or rather, parts of it because the rest is in documents. Is there any area that you consider to be significant that we perhaps did not cover with these examples?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it has to do with the question put by Judge Bonomy. I would like to say a few things. As far as I know, from the beginning of March 1998 the command of the Pristina Corps and the commander of the Pristina Corps personally, at that time General Pavkovic, visited Albanian villages, several villages at that. It was shown on television, so it was broadcast in public. They talked to Albanians with a view to giving political solutions a chance. These problems were solvable. An armed conflict would be the worst option at that. And secondly, that there would be no harm coming to them from the army and that they should not be allowed to be dragged into a fratricidal war. They said to General Pavkovic then and the team that was with him that they were facing terrible problems and pressures of being armed by force, that they were fighting against receiving these weapons because they did not want to take up arms against the Serbs who were the local population just like they were from way back. Another example, and it was the security organs that were particularly engaged in this respect and I'm sure that you'll have witnesses to testify about that. People went to a lot of villages and talked to Albanians who were armed by force and who returned these weapons, or rather, surrendered these weapons of their own free will and military and state organs were informed about this. Probably in these contacts that I talked about, they presented this to the international community, what it was that was going on there, and what the problems were. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now I would like us to move on to the period from October until the beginning of the war. Primarily I would like to deal with a few excerpts from documents that have to do with the KLA taking over parts of the territory, or rather, the return of the KLA to territories that were left by the security forces, the Yugoslav security forces, or rather, the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to that, I would like Exhibit 1020 to be shown, 3D. 3D1020, point 1.2 on this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, let us just make an introduction in order to take the Trial Chamber to the relevant period. It's the 11th of November, 1998, the time in the immediate aftermath of the signing of the October agreement between Milosevic and Holbrooke.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry if I said "signing," Your Honours, achieving an agreement, achieving an agreement, that might be a better word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I take it you're still looking for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, tell me what can we see from this document? It's a biggish paragraph, isn't it, it refers to quite a few things, but let us deal with it briefly.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I say one sentence. After the agreement was reached between Mr. Holbrooke and Milosevic, I think this was on the 13th of October and this agreement envisaged that the Army of Yugoslavia would withdraw to barracks except for three company-rank combat groups that remained in the area. This time vacuum between the moment when the agreement was reached and before the moment of arrival of the verification mission came was taken advantage of by the KLA. They took up their old positions, the positions they held before the anti-terrorist action had been launched. So they were back again. So now I'm commenting on what you're asking me about, roads and activities of the KLA vis-a-vis citizens, the army, MUP, and everyone moving along these roads, that is to say there are armed incursions, attacks, sabotage. Only between the 9th and 10th of November seven such KLA actions were registered along the Pristina-Nis road, the road to Podujevo as well and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General, would you please look at the same document, 1.4 and 1.5. In the English page that is page 2.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In those two paragraphs, 1.4 and 1.5, the document speaks about the establishment of armed check-points. The KLA established armed check-points in the areas of roads leading to villages where it checked IDs of the population, the civilians moving in that area, and seized, not to say robbed, their private property. The objective of this action was to show that they were in power, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in paragraph 1.5 I chose this incident because of its location.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the village of Racak in the municipality of Stimlje. The KLA members blocked it entirely. They controlled every exit and entry point into this village and out of this village, mistreating the citizens, the villagers of ethnic -- Albanian ethnic background who dared to move out of this village, threatening them with more radical measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Once again this is a document dated 11th of November, 1998. I would now like to -- I would now like you to look at the document 3D1025. Now we are one month ahead. The date is the 6th of December, 1998, and I think that it would be of interest for the Trial Chamber. Here we see that the KLA activities are talked about in the territory of the Podujevo municipality. This is the so-called Lap area, Lap zone of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The contents of this document are, indeed, very interesting because this document talks about the fortifications, the fortification works in the area of the Pristina-Podujevo road leading further north to Kursumlija. Two lines of trenches were made 60 centimetres wide and 1.7 metres deep. These trenches are manned by the best soldiers the KLA has wearing black uniforms, which means that they were members of the special units.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please make a pause here. I would like to draw the Chamber's attention to the following. These data were obtained from a person who had spent three months with the Kosovo Liberation Army. It is a soldier from the 2nd Army who had been captured during the previous bout of fighting in 1998?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and he is the original source.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So to speak, this is a man who spent three months with them who had inside information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And a part of this document, lest we should confuse the Chamber, refers to the time-period before the October agreement, but what I am interested in is this period December of 1998 and that would be on page 2 of the Serbian version, and it is also page 2 in the English version. So we will not go into any details, the trenches, the roads, the fortified firing positions that the KLA had set up in order to establish control of this road. This witness provided information about the unit deployed in this area and its intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that would be the last three paragraphs of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Or rather, that would be the last five paragraphs in the English version?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, but this document indicates that the -- that they're using women and children to build fortifications.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And you said that this had been a special unit, and in this paragraph here we see that this person noted in particular that as for -- that he also stressed what the intentions of the KLA were vis-a-vis this territory?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In a portion of this text he names persons who were, in his opinion, the commanders of these forces, among them is a person by the name of Remi. General, do you know who that is because several verifiers spoke about this person?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Rrustemi Mustafa, a.k.a. Remi, commander of the Lap zone. As far as I know he had been sentenced to 12 or 15 years in prison by the UNMIK courts, and he's serving a sentence in Dubrava prison and recently some prisoners escaped this prison. It was probably organised by the KLA, and Remi was among those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we're not interested in recent activities in that area. This opens doors that lead to passages we do not wish to explore.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not my intention. I wanted to ask the witness something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... You can control the witness. Can you also clarify for me whether the information that you're now leading from the witness relates to the period earlier than the report or does it relate to the period of the report? You referred to an infiltrator who was there for a period of three months.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the way I read this document, it is quite clear that the second half of the document pertains to the time-period immediately before this statement was taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And then towards the end there's a reference to the name of the provider of the information; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The very end and the beginning of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is this the infiltrator?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, he was a prisoner of the KLA. He was held captive by them for three months, so he spent three months with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I may have used the wrong expression, but this is the person you say was from the 2nd Army and was there for three months?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a person, as indicated in this document, had been a soldier of the 2nd Army and he was taken prisoner in this zone and spent some time after that with the KLA in this zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The circumstances in which he was captured, perhaps I can explain this, have nothing to do with the 2nd Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not necessary, but for some reason I have the impression that you said or the witness said that the period of three months was earlier, prior to October; is that wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The period of three months preceded the 6th of December, which means that it would also include parts of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And if I may add, there is other evidence about this group and its activities in this period, and our Defence may call this evidence or perhaps the Defence of other accused may do that as the Defence case proceeds. So this information will be corroborated by information from other sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could we move on to the next document, 3D1034, paragraph 2.1. General, now we're moving to the territory of the municipality of Glogovac, and this is the 22nd of December, 1998, and here we see that this is about the pressure. I will not be reading this document. I will just be making the most salient points. Paragraph 2.1 speaks about the pressure on the part of the KLA against the population, that includes threats, intimidation of Albanians who in any way show their loyalty to the state. There are some rather penal examples here, paying the electricity bills, registering their vehicles, and so on. And open promises that the KLA would soon establish its own authorities, and we have very clear deadlines for the attacks or actions that the KLA will launch in order to try to force the remaining Serbian authorities from Glogovac and put it under its full control. General, could you please tell me first of all what KLA unit was operating in the Glogovac municipality area?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know -- in fact, I don't really understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what operations zone of the KLA covered the municipality of Glogovac?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the Nerodimlje or Pastrik Operational Zone, but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps who was the commander of that zone or can you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I can't recall now.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if I can make one comment, if you allow me, just one sentence. This is about the organised rallies in Albanian villages organised by the KLA representatives with the aim of winning over the Albanian population of -- turning them into a homogenous entity in order to promote their terrorist and separatist goals on the one hand, and on the other hand the efforts to distance themselves from the official authorities of Serbian and Yugoslavia and to obstruct them in some way, trying to present themselves as the actual and future power structure in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And this is all happening in late December at the time when the verification commission is already in the field and when all parties are trying to calm the situation down and to achieve a political solution?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next document is 1035, 3D1035, paragraph 2.3, that would be on page 2 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is one not referred to in the statement, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 76.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please comment on this request or this demand sent by the KLA to KDOM and the verification mission?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in two sentences. So this is a communique from the KLA Main Staff, in which they, in fact, issue an ultimatum to the verification mission and KDOM, demanding that the MUP forces de facto pull out from the territory of Kosovo. This is not first such demand. I can give you --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: There's no need for you to give us such example. The document speaks for itself. Is this in line with what was achieved by the so-called October agreement?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Once again, the date of this document is the 24th of December, 1998. We will be getting back to this document relating to another case, and now I would like you to look at 3D1038. This is a document dated the 29th of December, 1998, paragraphs 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4. General, this document talks about the KLA's intention to set up a larger operational unit to control the Pristina-Podujevo road; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In 2.4 there is a description of the first combat line of these KLA forces that are right by the Pristina-Podujevo road. Also, there is a reference to the forces, or rather, there is a description of the forces that are at that locality. General, does this correspond to what the captured soldier had told the security organs almost a month before that in the document that we've just seen?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a confirmation of that information presented by the captured soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, this exhibit is referred to on page 18 of the statement, paragraph 60. Is the reference there to March 1999 inaccurate?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I give an explanation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, where is the reference in the document to the March 1999 spring offensive?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this document there is no mention, but it is mentioned in other documents and I think that -- well, I don't want to interpret what the witness wanted to say. Perhaps we should ask him why he said "March" there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, please let me finish speaking to the Judge.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, would you look at your own statement, paragraph 60. General, in paragraph 60 when you wrote the so-called spring offensive of March 1999, did you mean this document, 3D1038, or rather, on the basis of what did you place the so-called spring offensive in that time-period?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this document where it says that through electronic surveillance information was received about intensive preparations on the part of the terrorists for action throughout Kosovo and Metohija, fleeing from mobilisation there is an increase in the Siptars moving out through Montenegro --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There is no need for that any longer. I think the Judge wanted to ask you why you said "March," when there is no reference to March in the document.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Bonomy is right. I did say March. On the basis of all the information that we had; namely, that this offensive was being prepared for March so what Judge Bonomy said is quite appropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And your information relates to the month of December; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. This information is from the month of December; however, electronic surveillance made it possible to obtain these data about the spring offensive. And as I knew of all the other information, speaking of March, I put March in here, although you are right. There is no explicit reference to March in the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just have one more document that I'd like to deal with before the break, but I would like to say that my next documents actually pertain to information containing the spring offensive. So I will be dealing with that when we continue. Please, 3D1048, point 2 and point 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the interpreters that we go through this slowly. 2.6 on page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document has not been translated yet, or rather, we don't have it in e-court yet. So we are briefly going to deal with only a few documents in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In 2.6 there is a reference to the village of Pirane, and I am going to read only the first characteristic sentence. "On instructions from the terrorists from the so-called KLA, a considerable number of inhabitants of the village of Pirane, Prizren, on the 27th of February this year abandoned their homes, so in the -- so about 30 families are there now, whereas the abandoned houses were taken by the members of this terrorist organisation." Further on it says who had organised that, and then the last part of this paragraph says: "The fact that the terrorists are based in it constitutes a permanent danger for the movement of members and units of the VJ, of organs of the MUP, and the civilian population."

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I ask the witness, I would just like to remind you that a Prosecution witness spoke about this village and I believe that we will be referring to statements made by that witness later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, my question is: Is this yet another example? Now we're in March, that is to say the 2nd of March, 1999, and the KLA is slowly jeopardizing the most important roads. And in this way they're trying to take control of the entire territory.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was always their strategic objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understood what you said correctly, now would be the right time to take the break, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Gajic, we have to have a break at this stage, that will be for half an hour, and we will resume at 11.00. Meanwhile, could you please leave the courtroom with the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have 3D1016 on e-court, please, 2.6, page 2 in the Serbian version and page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, towards the end of the first session Judge Bonomy asked you about the spring offensive that the KLA was preparing. We have a document from the 5th of November, 1998, before us now. Can you tell me now on the basis of 2.6 what kind of information was the security administration of the General Staff receiving concerning KLA intentions in the period ahead from November onwards, that is?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first information about intentions to carry out a spring offensive, rather, they were talking about a long guerilla war, that is what they called it, in spring 1998. The security administration had that as early as October, mid-October I should say. Through our sources the -- this information was confirmed, and at some point the military intelligence department sometime in mid-November received confirmation of this through their own channels. What was pointed out was that this would take place in the spring, in March, a long guerilla war.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 4.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, the transcript, if you look at line 8 should, I think, be spring 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you continuing with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Paragraph 4.1, the same document, page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, you will probably notice that in this paragraph there is a reference to March for a planned general uprising.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, who is B. Bukoshi mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bujar Bukoshi who was prime minister of the illegal government of the Republic of Kosovo with its seat in Germany. He is a member of the moderate stream of the late Ibrahim Rugova.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to be shown document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before you do that can we go back to the first page of this document, please. Do you have the first page in front of you now, Mr. Gajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Paragraph 1, referring to the situation on the state border, says that there were no provocations or border incidents on the state borders with Albania and Macedonia guarded by the border units of the Pristina Corps. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did border units of the Pristina Corps guard the border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They had taken up the border posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to say that they secured the state border, and they were located in the border posts that had been built there, as is the case anywhere else in the world; that is to say that they controlled the state border, these border posts controlled the state border and prevented illegal crossings, smuggling, and other violations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We have the impression that this was the Ministry of the Interior that operated on the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I would like an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, can you say? Can you answer the Judge?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is called the line security of the border, and that was carried out by the Army of Yugoslavia. As for the in-depth security, that was carried out by MUP units; however, later that was changed bearing in mind the change that took place. I think that Mr. Cucak, Colonel Cucak spoke about that. As far as I can remember there were two extensions of the border belt and what the border actually was. I think it was 5 kilometres and 10 kilometres, but I'm sure that Colonel Cucak explained that properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we're moving in the completely wrong direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, how is it that you're aware of the evidence of Mr. Cucak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I followed the broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I give you an explanation for the border?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: By asking questions, yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- there's some confusion of some kind because the -- I think the evidence to this stage- and you can certainly find it in the record- is real clear that the army was in charge --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, please sit down and we'll hear the version that this witness wishes to give us. Mr. Visnjic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell me, do you know who controlled the border crossings on the overall territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, including the borders with Kosovo and Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the MUP controlled the border crossings.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And who was tasked with controlling the rest of the border?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell me, the border battalions that were tasked with controlling the border, the military border battalions, they were part of what units?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were part of the Pristina Corps, if we're talking about Kosovo specifically and if we're talking about the other parts of the border they were part of those units corps-strength units, that covered the appropriate zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, was this clear enough or should I pursue it any further?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The only uncertainty that remains in my mind now is the reference to the in-depth security which the witness says was originally the responsibility of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, when the border belt was narrow, a hundred to 500 metres, who was able to perform the in-depth control of the border?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In what belt?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that belt that you just mentioned. MUP had other jobs, regular jobs, regular work that it did further in the depth. As far as I know, the line security is what it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That point remains uncertain. Mr. Ackerman, what was it you wished to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Nothing now. The witness said what I was going to say, Your Honour, it had to do with the MUP was in charge of the border crossings, but the army was in charge of the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that is indeed our understanding of the situation, and it was complicated by the first paragraph of the letter. The explanation has been given, but the reference to in-depth security being the subject -- or being the area of responsibility of the MUP initially is unclear. But please continue, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence Exhibit 3D1027, paragraph 2.3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If when you're referring to an exhibit the point that you're making is somewhere in the statement, it would be helpful to be directed to the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that it will be a problem for me at this point in time, but I can give you a table later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, I can do that myself and I understand the problem. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: So, General, this is a report from the 9th of December, 1998, paragraph we're looking at is 2.3. Again, it is stated here that several thousand members of the KLA who had undergone training are preparing for action, and this time it is stated as one of the factors that would enable them to actually operate there the improvement of the weather and now we're talking about the spring of 1999; am I right?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Well, according to you, or rather, perhaps this is too broad a question. But why was it favourable for the KLA to launch an offensive in spring and not before, in light of the weather conditions?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the weather conditions are more favourable. If we're talking about camouflage, there are leaves on the trees so you can camouflage things on the ground and also spring comes after winter, there's no more snow. The border with Albania is specific in this respect, and I think there are some other circumstances that affected their choice of that period because all the other preparations were planned in such a manner that they should be completed by that time, spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like Defence Exhibit 1035, paragraph 1.1. 3D1035, paragraph 1.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, the information contained in this paragraph, this document is dated the 24th of December, 1998, was obtained from a person who had illegally crossed the border and who had been captured?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In the course of giving this statement, he told the investigators that he had been registered as a KLA fighter and that he had been in training. Could you please comment on paragraph 2, the last four lines, or rather, paragraph 1.1 and there you see the second passage in that very same paragraph, 1.1. And there it says what the KLA members were told while they were in training?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, we have the confirmation of what we had known and what I stated here, that Tropoje was one of the key training centres for the KLA troops. Second, that officers of the Albanian army took part in the training, and I think that I already answered your question, in fact, when I -- actually, this member of the KLA who had undergone training was told to go home to wait for the call-up and that they were being trained for large-scale clashes that would take place in the early spring.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now look at paragraph 2.1 in the same document, that would be on page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell me, what is ob 14 kog mentioned in the first line?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the security organ of the 14th counter-intelligence group --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let's take it slow. Where was this counter-intelligence group stationed?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Pristina, and it covered Kosovo and Metohija operationally.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, this intelligence group, did it have information from a meeting that took place in Switzerland? Could you please tell me in general how this intelligence group could have obtained this information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It had its operational positions. It was its task to carry out offensive operations in the territory and to engage operative sources that would target the centres where all the activities against the army and the defence of the country were being organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- well, this paragraph speaks for itself. I will not be reading it or analysing it, but we have here in detail what proposals were made to the KLA for its strategy in the forthcoming period.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: One interesting piece of information, General, here, it is stated that the KLA should put under its control broader parts of the territory in order to create conditions for the supply of weapons by air?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What does this refer to, because at that time the KLA did not have an air force?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well foreign -- it's foreign allies.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the Defence Exhibit 1038, paragraph 2.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: This is the document dated the 29th of December, 1998, and this time we're talking about preparations for the mobilisation. It's a new element in the preparations of the KLA; am I right, General?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Everything, again, is linked with the spring offensive?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have 1041 on the screen, paragraph 2.2. This is a document dated the 19th of January. We don't have the translation. Could we please see paragraph 2.2 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I can't see that paragraph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: It says: "Unverified intelligence from ob kvo Pristina indicate that the inhabitants in the settlements in the Karadacke area are preparing for the reception of refugees from the areas of Pristina, Urosevac, and Podujevo in case the situation should escalate." General, first of all if you have unverified intelligence, what does it mean?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means that the intelligence needs to be further verified. That's the raw data that cannot be taken as accurate, further determination is necessary to determine the actual state of affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 19th of January did the Army of Yugoslavia plan any military operations against the KLA in the area of Pristina, Urosevac, and Podujevo, do you know anything about that, in the period preceding the 19th of January and on the 19th of January in light of this time-frame?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about that in detail. There may have been some plans, bearing in mind the fact that after the agreement was signed there was an escalation, and it was getting closer to the end game.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, do you know whether anything was planned in the Pristina area at all?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next exhibit is 1050, paragraphs 2.1 and 2.2, 3D1050. This is a document dated the 5th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: First, in paragraph 2.1, General, what do we see here?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here we see in fact the confirmation of the earlier data that we have already seen, that in the KLA the training and all the other activities involved the active participation of the Albanian army troops and that some orders had been issued to the effect that all Albanian men fit for service should take part and the preparations for the war, building bunkers, digging trenches, fortifying the terrain in a word.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: This looks like some sort of a mobilisation; am I right, General?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at the same document, item 2.2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: This pertains to a different territory?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is about Sami Ljustak, one of the leaders or commanders of the KLA, and about the order to evacuate the civilian population at the foothills of Cicavica, that's to the west of Pristina, and to relocate the population to the Vucitrn area. Again, this is part of the preparations that I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And finally at the end of this paragraph we have the military mobilisation that the KLA is carrying out?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: And this is now the beginning of March 1999. Now I would like you to look at document 1052, 3D1052. This document is dated the 13th of March, paragraph 2.2.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO GAJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is about the forcible mobilisation on the part of the KLA, it's in the village of Korisa, in the Prizren municipality, on the 11th of March and the 12th of March the villagers were forcibly mobilised and that was just before the NATO aggression, and their training as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
